author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner list treats a page below 1 as the first page
summary: Opening the owner list with a requested page below 1 shows the error page today. The owner list must instead answer with its first page and a normal successful response, as the owner's bug report states.
acceptance_criteria: given a requested page of 0, when the owner list is opened, then the response succeeds (HTTP 200) and shows the first page of owners, the same as a request for page 1
given a negative requested page, when the owner list is opened, then the response succeeds (HTTP 200) and shows the first page of owners
given a requested page of 1 or above, when the owner list is opened, then the behavior is unchanged
non_goals: a requested page beyond the last page
notes: Owner request (intake line 1): 'the owner listing treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.' Observed cause: the owner controller subtracts 1 from the requested page and builds a page request from the result, so page 0 or below yields a negative page index and the request fails. The fix normalizes a request parameter, which docs/architecture-principles.md (Web controller row) places in binding, not in a business rule. test_names is one data-driven test covering page 0 and a negative page; the PRD gains Done-when bullet REQ-OWN-005 and Owner records edge case 4. The non_goals record deliberate omissions for this slice only, not new Non-Goals rows: the bug report names only pages below 1 on the owner list. No Non-Goals row is changed.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by docs/architecture-principles.md § Web controller row: clamping a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule. The fix therefore lands in OwnerController (docs/system-design.md § Contracts, OwnerController row, now also implementing REQ-OWN-005) and does not extend the recorded controller-business-rule deviation. Cause confirmed by grep (weaker basis, IDE oracle not connected): OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName builds PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize), which throws for page < 1. Normalize the bound page to at least 1 once, at the handler entry of processFindForm, before both the repository query and addPaginationModel. That way the rendered currentPage and the queried page agree.
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch and binding for GET /owners?page=0 and a negative page (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy, the one sanctioned mock). Assert HTTP 200, view owners/ownersList, and currentPage equal to 1.

Repository boundary: OwnerControllerTests already stubs OwnerRepository with Mockito. Extending that existing stub is tolerated, per docs/testing-principles.md mocking policy, to keep the test in the established controller-test seam. Verify the stub receives page index 0, the same as for page=1.
Binding: the existing int page request parameter (default 1) stays the binding target; no new entry point, no new bound type.

patterns.description: Existing request-parameter normalization in the same handler: lastName null-to-empty and strip, done before the query. The page clamp follows the same shape.

risks.risk: Normalizing only inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName would leave addPaginationModel rendering currentPage 0 or negative, which breaks the pagination links.
risks.mitigation: Clamp once at the handler entry so a single normalized value feeds both the query and the model (architecture-principles § Web controller: binding happens before delegation).

risks.risk: Owner list paging path: docs/system-design.md has no § Scale and Load row, and this slice adds no path that scales with data, only a range clamp on an existing page index.
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form, a Math.max-style clamp; page size and query are unchanged.

notes: Design-doc write: REQ-OWN-005 joined the OwnerController Contracts row. Non-goals respected: VetController has the same page - 1 shape but is out of scope for this slice (prd-entry non_goals); it is not to be touched. No design-doc-autofix records were present to audit.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The stub `findByLastNameStartingWith("", PageRequest.of(0, 5))` copies the production page size (`int pageSize = 5;` at OwnerController.java:136) into the test. If the page size changes, the stub stops matching and this test fails with a null-return error that does not point at the clamping rule. Only the page index (0) is the behavior under test here, so the test should not hard-code the page size.
findings.fix: Stub on the page index alone, e.g. match the Pageable with `argThat(pageable -> pageable.getPageNumber() == 0)`, or name the page-size literal as a Tier-1 constant derived from the same source the controller uses. Keep the `currentPage == 1` model assertion.

findings.description: The new test builds `new PageImpl<>(List.of(george(), new Owner()))`, a raw `new Owner()` with no name for its role. The extra blank owner is irrelevant to the assertions (status, view name, currentPage), and testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction requires new tests to build through a named factory from the start. The line was copied from the neighbouring test at line 149 (`grep -n 'new Owner()'` also lists line 191), which predates the brief and is not a pattern to repeat.
findings.fix: Use `new PageImpl<>(List.of(george()))`, reusing the existing `george()` helper at line 76 and dropping the irrelevant second owner.

approved_aspects: ./gradlew test --tests '*OwnerControllerTests*' ran green (BUILD SUCCESSFUL). The new parameterized test covers both inputs of PRD edge case 4 (0 and -1), as listed by `grading.py coverage-map --feature REQ-OWN-005` (declared test present, 1 of 1).
The test name theOwnerListShouldShowTheFirstPageForAPageBelowOne follows the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school and states the Done-when bullet.

Placement is correct: system-design.md row `OwnerController` (line 95) assigns request handling and paging to the web controller, and the clamp `Math.max(requestedPage, 1)` at OwnerController.java:98 is request normalization, so a MockMvc test is the right level. No production helper was widened for the test.

The test would fail if the clamp were removed: page=0 or -1 makes `PageRequest.of(page - 1, ...)` throw, so it guards the defect. It uses @ParameterizedTest/@ValueSource, AssertJ-compatible MockMvc matchers, no phase comments, and a straight-line body. The Mockito stub follows the host file's existing idiom (tolerated per the brief).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: The change sits at the trust boundary and makes input validation stronger, not weaker. OwnerController.java:98 `int page = Math.max(requestedPage, 1);` clamps the request-derived page before it reaches `PageRequest.of(page - 1, pageSize)` (OwnerController.java:137). That removes the IllegalArgumentException path a page of 0 or below used to trigger. Previously that exception reached the error page, which renders the exception message (docs/security-principles.md, secret-disclosure row).

No check is removed or weakened. The `@RequestParam` type stays `int`, so a non-numeric page still fails type conversion exactly as before. The `name = "page"` attribute keeps the external parameter name unchanged after the Java parameter was renamed to `requestedPage`.

Data access still goes through the derived repository query `findByLastNameStartingWith(lastname, pageable)` (OwnerController.java:138). No request value is concatenated into query text. The clamped `currentPage` model attribute is an int, so it adds no markup or escaping surface.

No new endpoint, binder, `@ModelAttribute` target, or allow-list change. The diff touches only the `processFindForm` signature and adds one local (changeset.py hunk on OwnerController.java). Mass-assignment posture is unchanged.
No secrets in the diff. The 4 changed files (2 docs, the controller, and its test) add no credential, token, key, or connection string (read in full from `python3 scripts/changeset.py`).

Supply chain: build.gradle is unchanged (`git diff --stat -- build.gradle` is empty) and no dependency was added. OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured (`grep -n -i dependencyCheck build.gradle` has no hits), so no NVD match ran in this review. Resolved runtime versions from `./gradlew dependencies`: Spring Boot 4.1.1 (spring-boot-thymeleaf), spring-webmvc 7.0.9, jackson-databind 3.1.5, thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE.

The upper bound is pre-existing and was not widened. A very large page stays within int arithmetic in `page - 1`, and Spring Data computes the offset as a long. This was not verified against Spring Data source in this review.
